_comment: Example staging document. It carries no credentials, no tenant hostnames
and no absolute local paths - only public, anonymously readable Microsoft
sample data. Copy it, point the entries at wherever the fixtures are
actually staged, and pass it to `python -m certification plan --staging`.
`hosts` becomes the safety gate's allowlist: a generated LOCATION that
resolves to any other host is refused before execution.
Blob paths are case-sensitive. A wrong-case directory fails with error
13807 (directory cannot be listed) rather than returning no rows, so keep
the casing exactly as the container reports it.
An `engine_local` entry is a path on the *engine host*, not on this
machine. Cells that read a file with no data source (C07, C11, C15) are
planned NOT_EXECUTABLE until one is supplied, because a client worktree
path handed to a server earns error 4860, not a certification result.
Every remote entry must declare a `shape`, naming an object in
scripts/certification/public_fixtures.py. The harness analyses a local demo
fixture and then reads a public blob, and those describe the same bytes
only if someone says so: without a shape the generated schema would be the
demo file's, projecting columns the public object does not have. A remote
entry with no declared shape is planned NOT_EXECUTABLE on purpose.
An `engine_local` entry needs no shape, because it means *these* fixture
bytes were copied to the engine host.

map, list, logical and decimal-boundary columns. The NYC taxi dataset has
21 flat scalar and timestamp columns and is NOT a substitute: mapping it
here would transfer the demo fixture's type-fidelity claims onto a file
that cannot support them. Those cells stay NOT_EXECUTABLE until the exact

_comment: The public iris CSV, five columns and 150 rows. It certifies the CSV
access pattern only: it has no Unicode, no boundary values and no wide
decimals, so it proves nothing about type fidelity. The demo
sales_scalars.csv keeps that job, statically.
A whole JSON object, read as one document. Its top-level keys are
image aliases Microsoft adds to over time, so the shape pins no
columns: the assertion is that the document arrives intact, which is
what SINGLE_CLOB is being certified for.
Newline-delimited JSON read through abs:// row framing - the exact
object the live run certified: 729 rows on both engines, four JSON
fields (timestamp, source, severity, message). An https
TYPE = BLOB_STORAGE source cannot read this, because that connector
rejects the delimiter options with error 5369; the https form is
recorded only so the negative case names a real object.
NYC yellow taxi, June 2018. Certifies the Parquet access pattern and
column projection against 21 documented columns. No row count is
asserted - a month of trips is millions of rows - so verification reads
TOP (10) and checks the column count.
